content.value_statement: Vue Options API projects often lose type safety and correct this binding. This skill gives focused rules for safer Vue 3 components.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Options API methods and lifecycle hooks need regular functions.
Shows how defineComponent improves TypeScript inference for Vue components.
Guides PropType usage for objects, arrays, functions, and union props.
Recommends strict TypeScript settings for safer this context.
Covers typed event handlers, computed return types, and provide or inject limits.
Highlights debounced or throttled method state that belongs in lifecycle hooks.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not an automated linter.
It focuses on Vue Options API, not Composition API migration.
It assumes the assistant can inspect the target Vue component files.
It does not guarantee runtime validation for PropType-only annotations.

use_cases.title: Fix this binding bugs
use_cases.description: Review Options API methods and lifecycle hooks so component data remains accessible at runtime.

use_cases.title: Improve component type inference
use_cases.description: Apply defineComponent, strict mode, PropType, and event parameter types to reduce any usage.

use_cases.title: Standardize Vue review guidance
use_cases.description: Use the references to flag risky patterns and suggest consistent Options API fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Check this binding
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Vue Options API component for arrow functions in methods or lifecycle hooks. Suggest regular function replacements.

prompt_templates.title: Add TypeScript safety
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this Vue 3 Options API component. Recommend defineComponent, strict TypeScript settings, and typed event handler changes.

prompt_templates.title: Harden props and computed types
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the props and computed options. Suggest PropType declarations, runtime validators where useful, and explicit computed return types.

prompt_templates.title: Audit legacy Options API patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these Vue Options API files for this binding, TypeScript inference, prop typing, provide or inject typing, and stateful method lifecycle issues.

output_examples.input: A component uses arrow functions for increment and mounted.
output: Flags both arrow functions because Vue cannot bind this to the component instance.
Recommends method shorthand for the method and lifecycle hook.
Notes that arrows remain safe inside callbacks that inherit this from a regular method.

output_examples.input: A TypeScript component has object props, untyped events, and computed totals.
output: Suggests defineComponent and PropType for the object prop.
Adds explicit event parameter types and target assertions.
Recommends a return type for the complex computed total.

output_examples.input: A legacy project uses TypeScript 4.5 with prop validators.
output: Recommends checking the TypeScript version before changing validators.
Suggests arrow validators for older TypeScript versions.
Explains that upgrading TypeScript can remove the legacy workaround.

best_practices: Use method shorthand for Options API methods and lifecycle hooks.
Enable strict TypeScript settings and wrap components with defineComponent.
Use PropType for complex props and add validators when runtime structure matters.
anti_patterns: Do not use arrow functions where Vue must bind this.
Do not rely on Object or Array constructors for complex TypeScript prop types.
Do not leave event handler parameters implicit in strict TypeScript projects.

faq.question: Does this skill support Vue 2?
faq.answer: Many this binding rules apply to Vue 2, but the examples focus on Vue 3 Options API.

faq.question: Does it convert components to Composition API?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on making Options API components safer and clearer.

faq.question: Can it fix TypeScript errors automatically?
faq.answer: It provides review guidance and suggested edits. The assistant must apply changes in your project.

faq.question: When should I use arrow functions?
faq.answer: Use arrows inside callbacks when they should inherit this from a regular Options API method or hook.

faq.question: Why use defineComponent?
faq.answer: defineComponent gives TypeScript the component shape needed for stronger inference in Options API components.

faq.question: Does PropType validate data at runtime?
faq.answer: No. PropType helps TypeScript. Add Vue validators when runtime object structure must be checked.
